examples.ko: 아버지는 마흔 살부터 새치가 나기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My father started getting gray hairs from the age of forty.
I found a gray hair while looking in the mirror.

examples.ko: 새치 때문에 염색을 해야 하나 고민돼요.
examples.en: I'm wondering whether to dye my hair because of the gray hairs.

examples.ko: 요즘 새치가 부쩍 늘어서 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: My gray hairs have increased a lot lately and it bothers me.

examples.ko: 머리를 빗다가 새치 몇 가닥을 뽑았어요.
examples.en: While combing my hair, I pulled out a few gray strands.
I'm young but have a lot of gray hair, which worries me.

explain: 나이가 많지 않은데 검은 머리 사이에 섞여 나는 흰 머리카락이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '흰머리'라고도 하고, '새치가 나다', '새치가 생기다'로 써요. '새치기'와 소리가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I looked in the mirror and plucked out a gray hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흰 머리카락을 뽑는다는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for plucking out a gray hair.

phrases.en: I went to the hair salon to dye my gray hairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흰머리를 덮으려고 머리를 물들이는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to dyeing hair to cover gray strands.

phrases.en: I've gotten a lot more gray hair lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 나이와 상관없이 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that is used more often in daily speech, regardless of age.

explain_en: It means white hairs mixed into dark hair when a person is not that old. In daily talk people also just say '흰머리', and it is used as '새치가 나다' or '새치가 생기다'. It sounds like '새치기' but is a completely different word.

examples.en: You stayed up all night, so how are you so fresh?
My grandfather is still full of energy despite his age.
After drinking coffee, my mind felt sharp.

examples.ko: 아침에 푹 자고 일어나면 쌩쌩한 기분이에요.
examples.en: When I wake up after a good sleep, I feel fresh.
I took a nap, so I worked energetically in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝났는데도 친구는 쌩쌩하게 놀러 갔어요.
examples.en: Even after the exam, my friend went out to play, full of energy.

explain: 친구나 가족끼리 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 밤을 새웠는데 멀쩡할 때나 나이 든 분이 건강해 보일 때 써요. '팔팔하다'는 힘이 넘치고 활발한 느낌이고, '쌩쌩하다'는 지치지 않고 상태가 좋다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: You look fresh even though you didn't sleep yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 지치지 않은 것처럼 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks not tired at all.

phrases.en: I'm not as lively as I used to be these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 기운이 예전만 못하다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In negative form, it says energy isn't what it used to be.

phrases.en: Grandma is still full of energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌩쌩하다'보다 힘이 넘치고 활발한 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense of being full of vigor than 쌩쌩하다.

explain_en: This is a casual word for friends and family. You use it when someone is fine after staying up all night, or when an older person looks healthy. '팔팔하다' feels full of power and activity, while '쌩쌩하다' feels not worn out and in good shape.

examples.en: I dyed my hair at home with hair dye.

examples.ko: 염색약 냄새가 너무 독해서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: The dye smell was so strong that I opened the window.

examples.ko: 염색약이 옷에 묻으면 잘 안 지워져요.
examples.en: If dye gets on your clothes, it doesn't come off easily.
I have a lot of gray hair, so I bought hair dye.
Be careful not to let the dye touch your skin.
I agonized over the dye color and chose brown.

explain: 주로 머리카락을 염색할 때 쓰는 약을 말해요. 옷감이나 천을 물들이는 재료는 보통 '염료'라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: I applied the hair dye evenly on my hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 염색할 때 약을 머리에 바르는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes putting dye on the hair when coloring it.

phrases.en: I bought hair dye at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 염색하려고 준비할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when preparing to dye hair at home.

phrases.en: Hair dye got on my clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 염색하다가 다른 곳에 묻었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when dye gets on something else by accident.

explain_en: It mainly means the product used to color hair. The material for coloring fabric or cloth is usually called '염료', which keeps the two apart.

examples.en: Fine lines form around my eyes every time I smile.
With makeup, fine wrinkles are less visible.

examples.ko: 화면이 너무 선명해서 얼굴의 잔주름까지 다 보여요.
examples.en: The screen is so sharp that even fine wrinkles on the face show.
I look older because of the fine lines.
Fine wrinkles have increased on the backs of my hands too.
I heard this cream is good for caring for fine lines.

explain: 눈가나 입가에 생기는 가늘고 작은 주름이에요. 깊게 패인 건 그냥 '주름'이라고 해요. '주름살'도 비슷하게 쓰고, '잔주름이 생기다/늘다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I've gotten fine lines around my eyes lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주름이 새로 보이기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wrinkles first start to appear.

phrases.en: As I get older, I get more fine lines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 있던 주름이 더 많아질 때 써요.
화장품이나 피부 관리 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about cosmetics and skin care.

explain_en: These are thin, small wrinkles around the eyes or mouth. Deep ones are just called '주름'. '주름살' is used similarly, and you say '잔주름이 생기다/늘다'.

en: to be slender; to be slim

examples.en: That actor is tall and slender.

examples.ko: 동생은 호리호리한 체격이라 옷이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: My younger brother is slim, so clothes look good on him.
He looks slim, but he's strong.
I exercise every day to keep a slender figure.
He is a slender young man with a fair face.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 호리호리했는데 지금은 많이 쪘어요.
examples.en: I was slim as a kid, but I've put on a lot of weight now.

explain: 키가 크면서 몸이 가늘고 날렵한 모습에 어울려요. '날씬하다'가 살이 적고 보기 좋다는 느낌이라면, '호리호리하다'는 길쭉하고 가는 몸매를 그려요. '마르다'는 때때로 걱정스러운 느낌이 있어서 말투가 달라요.

phrases.en: I envy that model's slender body.

phrases.example: 검은 옷을 입으면 더 호리호리해 보여요.
phrases.en: You look slimmer when you wear black clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I work out, so I'm not slender anymore.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the body is not slim.

explain_en: It suits a body that is tall, thin, and lithe. '날씬하다' feels like being slim in a nice way, while '호리호리하다' paints a long, slender build. '마르다' can sound worrisome, so the tone is different.
